note: How Ostrel opens up. The world is ten lands, each its own map, joined by ways: roads that leave one land at its edge and come into the next. A way is shut until the story opens it (from a stage, or with the flag open.<way id>), and something Rhea can see stands across the road while it's shut: snow, a Guild checkpoint, a shut gate. 'why' is what she's told when she walks up to it. Everything inside a land Rhea can reach is open. Finds are rare things lying on a land's map from a stage until picked up.

cloudline-vale.why: The mountain road down to the vale.

cloudline-north.why: Snow chokes the high passes. Nobody gets through to the north until the thaw.

cloudline-vael.why: The spire ridge vanishes into thick cloud. Without someone who knows the way, Rhea would walk straight off the edge.

vale-north.why: Drevka clan riders watch the high grazing at the top of the drove road. Strangers who come uninvited don't come back down.

vale-west.why: The Free Towns have shut their gates to strangers from the north since the raids.

vale-east.why: League toll-men hold the hill road. Nobody without a Corvane letter gets past the toll house.

vale-millcities.why: A Guild checkpoint closes the road south to the Millcities. Without indenture papers, Rhea would be taken at the barrier.

west-coast.why: Smugglers watch the coast road to Port Ashby, and they don't like new faces.

west-millcities.why: A Guild checkpoint closes the canal road into the Millcities.

east-ember.why: Beyond here is a week of desert. Nobody crosses it without water, a guide and a reason.

millcities-heartland.why: Vantry's outer wall, and the Guild's own Wardens on the gate. Not yet.

finds.text: Duskwort, growing wild on the old monastery terraces. Healers dry a sprig to keep their hands steady.
A drove bell, lost in the grass above the camp. Kith settle to the sound of it.
A brass indenture number, thrown from the cart. Nobody was ever stamped with it.
A tray-iron from the burnt brood house, cooled in the ditch. Heavy enough to forge into something.
A bundle of boiled linen in the grass by the road, dropped from some pedlar's pack.
A twist of willowbark in waxed paper, wedged in the cairn at the top of the climb. Left for whoever needs it.
A small pot of honey salve, sealed with wax, set on a fence post. Someone's kindness to travellers.
Clean bandages in an oilcloth roll, fallen from a cart.
Willowbark, stripped and drying on a stone. Whoever left it has gone on.
